rows.12:120c4:
You're going to stop editing?
I see. When someone involved in an independent film has died, I understand why you can't help thinking that way.
He'd finally founded the Film Research Society he'd longed for and gotten to the point of actually making a film, so he was bitterly disappointed too.
He was a warm-hearted person, so he decided to give up editing the film.
Besides, he was reluctant to edit a movie that showed a person who'd been murdered.{p}
rows.12:12694: I see. So you can't keep up with Tokita's way of doing things either, {a}, just as I thought.{p}
rows.12:126f0:
And then Taichi Nakayama, the one he trusted most, said he was quitting too.
He was the one who'd been shooting the film with the 8mm camera.
He was in the same year as Tokita, too.
Tokita was stunned.
He'd thought that Nakayama, at least, would stick with him.
And Nakayama had always agreed with Tokita's way of thinking.
"I thought you of all people wouldn't quit on me! Why☆"
Tokita shouted.
"You're way too wrapped up in this film.
Have you ever thought about how much you're jerking everyone around?"
Nakayama told him.
You can see there's no use saying anything to Tokita when he's this worked up, right?
Tokita talked Nakayama around and finally got him to stay in the society.{p}
